subject: PoC scope & competitive checklist — MedLytics discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@medlytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-08-16T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: PoC scope & competitive checklist — MedLytics discovery follow-up

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side so we have a shared source of truth and a clear next-step plan. If anything below is off, flag it and I’ll update.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- Latency variability on current endpoints causing timeouts in the live triage UI (95th percentile spikes to ~1.2s).
- High per-token cost when processing batches of patient notes; you want predictable unit economics.
- Need for an auditable trail of model inputs/outputs for internal compliance reviews.

Top goals for a 6–8 week PoC:
1) Reduce tail latency to < 350ms for 95th percentile under your typical traffic profile (50–200 RPS burst).
2) Demonstrate cost savings of at least 30% on comparable throughput vs your current provider.
3) Show end-to-end auditability (request IDs, immutable logs, and retention controls).

Competitive context we discussed:
- You’re running a parallel evaluation against GaleAI and NimbusServe. Key decision criteria you spelled out were latency SLOs, cost at scale, and control over model versions.
- You’ll give a slight preference to vendors who can support private deployment in your VPC for PHI-sensitive flows.

Proposed PoC tests (what we suggest running):
A) Latency stress runs: replicate your 50/200 RPS traffic profile with 95th/99th percentile reporting and cold-start characteristics.
B) Cost model run: measure tokens-per-inference and projected monthly cost under your real workload mix.
C) Auditability check: demonstrate request-level logging, KMS integration, and a short retention policy toggle.

Deliverables we’ll provide by week 1 of the PoC:
- PoC plan & acceptance criteria (attached: MedLytics_PoC_Spec_v1.pdf)
- Competitive matrix template (attached: redwood-competitive-matrix.csv)
- Sandbox endpoint credentials + onboarding checklist

Asks from you to kick off:
- Confirm the three PoC acceptance criteria above and the final list of test datasets (sanitized).
- Provide a point of contact on infra who can open the VPC peering and KMS details (I think Rajesh might own this?)
- Target start date window (we mentioned aiming for Aug 24–28).

I’ll loop in Marissa to align on measurement dashboards and Vanessa to confirm any special pricing for a short-term reserved test pool.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Connor
Connor Obrien
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0198

Subject: Re: PoC scope & competitive checklist — MedLytics discovery follow-up

Connor —

Thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with our notes. A few clarifications and constraints from our side:
- The 350ms 95th target is aggressive but acceptable as a stretch goal; we’ll evaluate results holistically (latency + cost).
- For datasets: we will share three sanitized batches (triage_notes_small.json, triage_notes_medium.json, triage_notes_large.json). Delivery ETA: Aug 20.
- Rajesh will be the infra POC for VPC/KMS; he’s copied for visibility.

Two quick asks: can Redwood run the first latency baseline without VPC peering (hosted sandbox) so we can get initial numbers before infra work is completed? And can you include a simple breakdown of where tail latency comes from (model, network, batching) in the deliverable?

Also, we’re reviewing internal procurement constraints — if there’s any standard paperwork you need early, please share.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Head of Clinical Product, MedLytics
alyssa.chen@medlytics.com

Connor / Vanessa —

Nice capture. A couple of internal notes before we move forward with the formal PoC doc: 
- Pricing: We can offer a time-limited reserved pool for PoC weeks 1–4 at 25% off list, plus a capped token estimate so MedLytics feels comfortable about spend. Vanessa, can you confirm if that discount needs AE approval or you can commit?
- Competitive angle: GaleAI appears to favor model-proxying to reduce integration work (less control), NimbusServe is pushing an on-prem appliance (higher infra lift). Highlighting Redwood’s hybrid option + transparent kernels/quantization approach should be favorable.
- Measurement: I’ll build a shared Grafana dashboard that pulls latency+cost metrics; need Connor to share realistic SLO windows and the sanitized dataset shape.

I’ll draft the acceptance criteria into the PoC spec after we confirm pricing cadence.

—Marissa

Great, thanks for the quick replies and confirmations. Quick updates and final next steps to get the PoC rolling: 
1) Sandbox baseline: yes — Marissa will spin up hosted sandbox endpoints this week so we can run the initial latency baseline without VPC connectivity. Expected baseline report by Aug 20.
2) Datasets: Alyssa — we’ll expect the three sanitized files on Aug 20; please upload to the Drive folder linked above.
3) Infra/peering: Rajesh — when your team is ready we’ll exchange VPC CIDRs and KMS key ARNs. I’ve added a short checklist in the Drive (network_onboarding.md).
4) Pricing: Vanessa — can you confirm whether the 25% PoC discount can be committed by EOD Aug 18? If not, please share the escalation path.
5) Measurement: Marissa will publish the Grafana dashboard and a short runbook for interpreting the 95th/99th percentile reports.

If all looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for a PoC kickoff on Aug 24 and attach the final PoC spec.

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.
